chats.answer:
For replacing a DVR while keeping your existing analog security cameras, I recommend looking at Dahua, Hikvision, and XMEye-compatible alternatives from established brands such as ANNKE.

The most important thing is to buy a hybrid DVR (often called an XVR) that supports your cameras' existing video format, rather than a standard IP-camera NVR.

A good replacement should offer:

BNC camera inputs so you can reuse your existing coaxial cables.

TVI, CVI, AHD, and CVBS support for compatibility with different generations of analog cameras.

H.265/H.265+ recording to save hard-drive space.

Remote viewing through a phone app.

8 or 16 channels, ideally with room for future expansion.

SATA hard-drive support for continuous local recording.

One important compatibility warning: If your existing cameras are older standard-definition analog (CVBS), a 4K DVR will not improve their image quality. It can still be a worthwhile upgrade for reliability, recording, and remote access. Also, Dahua and Hikvision have U.S. regulatory restrictions relevant to some installations, so that may affect the choice.

chats.answer:
If you want to replace your existing security DVR without replacing your analog cameras or running new cables, I recommend looking at a hybrid DVR/XVR that supports multiple analog video standards.

The best options are generally from Dahua, Hikvision, and Uniview, depending on your cameras and how many channels you need.

The most important consideration is compatibility. Many older analog cameras use CVBS (standard definition), while newer analog HD cameras use TVI, CVI, or AHD. Not every DVR supports all of these formats.
